summary.oneLiner: TeamLease delivered resilient profit growth (PAT +22% YoY) despite a significant revenue drag from a single NBFC client in-sourcing 20k associates, proving the efficacy of its operating leverage and cost-to-hire reduction strategies. The approved INR buyback and strong cash position (INR 600cr) signal capital discipline, while the strategic pivot toward high-margin GCC, AI-skills, and apprenticeship models positions the firm to capture India's workforce formalization tailwinds in FY27.

one-line thesis: TeamLease delivered resilient profit growth (PAT +22% YoY) despite a significant revenue drag from a single NBFC client in-sourcing 20k associates, proving the efficacy of its operating leverage and cost-to-hire reduction strategies. The approved INR buyback and strong cash position (INR 600cr) signal capital discipline, while the strategic pivot toward high-margin GCC, AI-skills, and apprenticeship models positions the firm to capture India's workforce formalization tailwinds in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,925cr (Q4, -2% QoQ due to NBFC in-sourcing); Full Year +6% YoY. EBITDA Margin: 1.5% (Q4, +10bps QoQ); Full Year 1.34% (+10bps YoY). PAT: +22% YoY (Q4), +33% YoY (FY26); includes INR 143cr tax refund one-off (underlying PBT +20% YoY). Order Book: ~20k open positions at FY27 start (+15-20% QoQ). Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash INR 600cr); One-offs include INR 143cr tax refund and INR 5.82cr provision for labor court exceptional item.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Recovery expected in H1 FY27 post planned exit of 10k low-margin headcount. Margin: Targeting >20% YoY EBITDA growth in FY27 driven by mix shift to Specialised/DA and operating leverage. Order Inflow: Strong pipeline with 20k open roles; focus on variable markup models. Capex/Commissioning: Low capex intensity; focus on tech/AI integration rather than heavy infrastructure.
order book & pipeline: ~20,000 open positions at start of FY27; recovered 70% of volume loss and 80% of recurring revenue loss from NBFC in-sourcing by year-end.
segment / subsidiary detail: General Staffing: 2.87 lakh associates (Q4), PAPM INR 689 (+20pts vs Q1); underlying business added 14k associates excluding in-sourcing. Specialised Staffing: 7,500 associates; GCC contributes 67% of segment revenue; Global business revenue +200% YoY. Degree Apprenticeship: +1,000 net adds in Q4; strong momentum in GCC/Manufacturing. HR Services: Full year EBITDA +22% YoY; Q4 seasonality impacted by EdTech billing timing.
growth verticals / optionality: Scaling GCC 'bot' models and RPO for higher realization; AI-led hiring tools productizing proprietary data; expansion of PMIS 3.0 internship scheme; formalization tailwind from new Labor Codes shifting share from unorganized to organized players.
margins & cost dynamics: PAPM improved to INR 689 (Q4) from INR 669 (Q1) driven by 70% new mandates on variable markup model and shift to mid-sized/higher-margin logos. Cost-to-hire reduced structurally by 20% YoY via tech/AI efficiencies and sourcing variabilization.
capex / expansion: Minimal traditional capex; investments focused on AI-enabled ATS, upskilling recruiters, and backend technology platforms to drive operating leverage without linear headcount increase.
capital allocation: Board approved buyback of up to 25% of free reserves at INR 1,600/share, funded by existing cash (INR 600cr); management cites undervaluation relative to earnings power. No major M&A announced; focus on organic scaling.
risks & watch-items: Transition costs and headcount slowdown in FY27 due to new Labor Codes implementation; geopolitical energy price inflation impacting client sentiment; concentration risk in BFSI sector despite diversification; potential regulatory notices (PF/GST) though management expresses high confidence in legal defense.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; new CEO Suparna Mitra emphasizes 'profitable growth' and 'operating leverage' over blunt volume; transparent about one-off headcount impacts but bullish on structural margin expansion and formalization trends.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'underlying' business actually grew headcount by 14k in FY26 despite reported decline, masking the strength of the core engine; 24% of Q4 gross joinees were first-time formal employees, highlighting the company's role in India's informal-to-formal labor shift which is underappreciated in pure revenue metrics.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Labor Codes increasing compliance burden for unorganized competitors | TeamLease Services Ltd | beneficiary | High | Management explicitly states 90% of industry is unorganized; new codes and Shram Suvidha Portal will force formalization, driving market share to compliant players like TeamLease. |
| NBFC in-sourcing reduced reported headcount | TeamLease Services Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Recovery of 80% of recurring revenue and 20k open roles suggests the in-sourcing was a one-off event, not a structural loss of client trust, setting up a low-base rebound in FY27. |
| Traditional IT hiring freeze | Generic IT Staffing Peers | loser | Med | Shift in demand is strictly toward AI/Cloud/Cybersecurity skills; peers lacking specialized GCC/AI capabilities may face margin compression while TeamLease pivots successfully. |

themes.title: Workforce solutions & facility management formalization
themes.need: Formalization, GCC hiring and compliance outsourcing drive staffing and integrated facility-management demand - QUESS/TEAMLEASE on flexi-staffing & GCC enablement; SIS/KRYSTAL/UDS on integrated security + facility management. Headcount additions and wage-bill growth are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: Net headcount additions; GCC/enterprise staffing wins; new FM contract ramps.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "TeamLease has established itself as an end-to-end people supply chain solutions provider, delivering integrated workforce solutions across the employee lifecycle", spanning "manpower sourcing, talent acquisition, workforce digitization, productivity enhancement, and compliance management" across the 3Es: Employment, Employability and E-workforce.
- The deck frames the four Labour Codes as the "most consequential regulatory shift for organized staffing in a generation" and reads it both ways: a structural positive because "a single central licence, uniform wage definitions, and mandatory formal appointment letters raise the compliance bar in a way that favours large, organized players like TeamLease over unorganized contractors", the core "formalization" thesis; but a "near-term cost/complexity" because "the 50%-of-CTC wage definition raises PF/gratuity cost per associate and requires payroll-system and contract rework across the client base".
- Scale claims: "4,000+ Employers served across the group", "26 Lakh+ People placed to date", "3.4 Lakh+ Associates & trainees", "7.5 Lakh+ Students", "28 States" and "7,500+ locations"; the journey slide describes "25 years from a four-office start-up to India's largest private-sector employer ambition" and notes that in 2021 it "Became India's largest IT staffing company by headcount".
- GCCs are called "the single largest driver of incremental staffing demand in India", with "67% of specialised staffing revenue originated from GCCs" and specialised staffing "the segment best positioned to capture GCC and technical-role demand".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leadership] "2026 ₹238 Cr buyback completed; new MD & CEO (Suparna Mitra) takes charge"; the board slide lists Ms. Suparna Mitra as Managing Director & CEO, Ashok Reddy as Executive Vice Chairman & Whole-Time Director, Narayan Ramachandran as Chairman & Non-Executive Non-Independent Director and Manish Sabharwal as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director.
- [Regulation] Labour Codes timeline: "21 Nov 2025 All four Labour Codes (Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security, OSH) notified as law, replacing 29 earlier central statutes"; "8 May 2026 Ministry of Labour & Employment notifies the Central Rules under all four Codes"; state rules "Vary by state, some finalized, others still in draft"; and ongoing "single central OSH licence for staffing firms replaces state-by-state registration".
- [Risk] "Watch-item: GCC linked demand is more discretionary to global technology capex cycles than blue-collar general staffing, a slowdown in global IT/tech spend is the main risk to this vector."
- [Corporate] Listed on BSE and NSE in 2016 (BSE: 539658 | NSE: TEAMLEASE | ISIN: INE985S01024); founded 2000; first PE investment from Gaja Capital in 2011-16.
